messages:
Alex (PM): quick question — for streaming chat/completions, customers keep asking about resumability and backpressure. do we want to standardize on SSE or WebSocket for the hosted API? what should the handshake look like?

Suresh (eng-runtime): short answer: both have pros. SSE = simpler (HTTP friendly, works through proxies), WS = richer (bidirectional, easier to signal ACKs/backpressure). main infra concern is LB idle timeouts for long-lived conns.

Ryan (eng): notes from the prototype: we tried SSE with a small meta event up front: `event: meta\ndata: {"protocol":"1.0","capabilities":["resume","finish_reasons"]}` then `event: delta\ndata: {...}`. resume implemented via per-delta `cursor` field.

Emily (devex): +1 to the `meta` event. SDKs can auto-detect EventSource vs WS and parse that. but browsers have native EventSource only for SSE; node fetch streaming is different — we need good examples.

Maria (research): finish reasons are tricky — model can emit `stop_token`, `max_tokens`, `user_cancelled`, `internal_error`. we should standardize the canonical set and include an optional `model_reason` string for debugging.

Ryan (eng): practical tradeoffs: SSE can't receive client-side control frames except closing the connection. to implement backpressure on SSE we had to chunk and rate-limit server side plus use a thin `ack` endpoint (POST /v1/stream/ack) where client posts last-seen cursor. Feels hacky.

Suresh (eng-runtime): with WS we can do real acks and windowing (like giving a token budget). also easier to implement resumability: include `resume_token` in every delta and on reconnect client sends `resume_token` and server either replays missing deltas or returns a `resync` snapshot.

Emily (devex): but WS compatibility is worse across corporate proxies and some cloud customers prefer plain HTTPS for compliance. SSE + ack endpoint is more likely to work out-of-the-box.

Alex (PM): makes sense. tradeoffs seem to be: SSE = compatibility, simpler infra; WS = feature-rich (acks, backpressure, resume). customers asking for resume looks like a high priority.

Ryan (eng): proposal: default public API uses SSE (easy onboarding), but we offer WS as an opt-in for dedicated/dedicated+customers who need resume/low-latency two-way control. protocol sketch: initial meta event (protocol/version/capabilities), then deltas with `cursor` and `resume_token`, and final `finish` event with `finish_reason` and `model_reason`. example:```\nevent: meta\ndata: {"protocol":"1","capabilities":["resume","finish_reasons","structured_output"]}\nevent: delta\ndata: {"cursor":123,"resume_token":"rt-abc","delta":"Hello"}\nevent: finish\ndata: {"finish_reason":"max_tokens","model_reason":"eos_token"}\n```

Maria (research): +1 for including `model_reason`. also recommend `quality_flags` array for downstream eval (e.g., `truncated`, `low_confidence`).

Suresh (eng-runtime): infra notes: make sure LB timeouts set to > 15m for SSE; implement connection-level heartbeat/ping. for WS we need sticky sessions or a shared session store for resume tokens.

deploy-bot: deploy note — our cloud LB default idle timeout is 60s. we'll need infra change before any long-lived SSE rollout.

Emily (devex): SDK ergonomics: unify API so customer code doesn't change between SSE/WS. e.g., `client.streamChat()` returns the same async iterator of events. SDK picks underlying transport. docs + cookbooks needed.

Alex (PM): decision criteria suggestion: 1) compatibility (browsers/proxies), 2) resume capability, 3) complexity for SDKs, 4) infra changes required, 5) customer priority. aim: ship SSE default w/ `meta` + `resume_token` + ack endpoint as MVP; ship WS opt-in for resume + backpressure in next quarter.

Ryan (eng): action items: - write RFC for protocol + canonical JSON schema for events - perf test SSE vs WS at 95th percentile token latency - implement `meta` event + `finish_reason` enumeration - prototype ack endpoint (SSE) and resume handshake (WS)

Suresh (eng-runtime): I'll start a small infra PR to raise LB timeouts and add a connection heartbeat.

Maria (research): I'll draft `finish_reason` enum and `model_reason` guidance (short list + examples).

Emily (devex): I'll draft SDK pseudocode and a migration guide.

Alex (PM): great. can we sync this into a short RFC? assign owners and target for next planning. thanks all :thumbsup:
